summary.headline: US AI safety centre staff told to report to the White House
summary.body: AP reported that staff at CAISSI, the US AI safety centre, were told to informally report to the White House, raising questions about its independence and pulling Alignment & Control down 0.28. Nvidia reportedly ordered cloud partners to keep 51% of capacity for non-Chinese clients, trimming Capability Velocity, and Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, prompting a board probe and a small rise in Catastrophic Risk. President Trump told 60 Minutes he is open to AI guardrails while framing AI as a race with China, lifting Global Coordination. Meta expanded AI age detection worldwide, raising Surveillance & Control. Protector God and Enslaved God fell; 1984 rose. Horizon Balance fell to -18.87 from -18.51.
summary.movers_note: Protector God -0.34, led by the CAISSI report (-0.17). Enslaved God -0.25, from the CAISSI report (-0.12) and Nvidia's capacity order (-0.09). 1984 +0.25, from Meta's age detection (+0.13) and Trump's guardrails remarks (+0.10).
coming_up: House briefing request to Jensen Huang, 18 Nov

events.title: Nvidia's Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy; board opens probe
events.summary: Jensen Huang told staff he had an affair with a Megaspeed executive US intelligence reportedly believes was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Nvidia's board opened an independent probe, and three House committee chairs requested a closed-door briefing on Nov 18.
events.reason: Alleged Chinese intelligence targeting of the top AI-chip CEO sharpens the US-China chip security fight; this is a governance scandal, not a capability change, so T1.

events.title: Nvidia reportedly orders cloud partners to keep 51% of capacity for non-Chinese clients
events.summary: The FT reports that Nvidia verbally told cloud partners worldwide that at least 51% of new services must go to non-Chinese firms, and it tightened tracking of Southeast Asian partners. Black-market B300 racks reportedly sold for $2.8M in China.
events.reason: Tighter limits on compute reaching China (F1 down for Chinese labs) deepen the tech-bloc split (F4 down); the rule is unconfirmed and narrow, so T1.

events.title: AP: US AI safety centre CAISSI staff told to informally report to White House
events.summary: Two former officials told the AP that staff at Commerce's CAISSI (about $10M a year, roughly one-eighth of the UK AISI's budget) were asked to informally report to a White House office. The centre has no permanent leader and stopped publishing safety reports by August.
events.reason: The US safety evaluator is losing independence and capacity (F3 down); the account rests on two anonymous sources, so T1.

events.title: Trump tells 60 Minutes he is open to AI guardrails but frames AI as a race with China
events.summary: In a 60 Minutes interview, Trump said AI risks can be managed, signalled openness to working with Democrats on safeguards, and repeatedly warned against falling behind China.
events.reason: Words only: a mild softening toward guardrails (F4 up slightly), offset by race framing, so T1.

events.title: Meta expands AI age detection worldwide across Instagram and Facebook
events.summary: Meta is extending AI age estimation globally, beyond the US, EU and Brazil, to move suspected 13-17-year-olds into teen accounts even if they gave adult birthdates. It is also bringing the system to Facebook, with Threads to follow.
events.reason: AI profiling of users' ages rolled out globally expands automated monitoring (F6 up); it is child-safety driven and limited in scope, so T1.
